quests.instruction: An upright cylinder, like a can, is seen from the side. Which flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: Picture the can's outline from the side: straight sides, a flat top, and a flat bottom.
quests.explanation: From the side, a cylinder has straight sides and a flat top and bottom, so it looks like a rectangle. From above, it looks like a circle.
quests.funFact: A label wrapped around a can becomes a rectangle when it is peeled off and laid flat.

quests.instruction: A cone stands on its flat base. Looking straight down on it from above, which flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: From above, you see the round base around the tip.
quests.explanation: From above, the round base forms the outline and the tip sits at the center, so a cone looks like a circle.
quests.funFact: From the side the same cone looks like a triangle, so one solid can show two different flat shapes.

quests.instruction: A square pyramid sits on a table. Looking straight down from above, what is the outline you see?
quests.hint: The outline of the view from above follows the shape of the base.
quests.explanation: The base of a square pyramid is a square, and the sloping sides fit inside it, so from above the outline is a square.
quests.funFact: Architects draw top views, called plans, to show the outline of a building.

quests.instruction: A cube is cut straight through the middle, parallel to one of its faces. What shape is the cut surface?
quests.hint: The cut surface is as wide and as tall as the faces of the cube.
quests.explanation: Each face of a cube is a square, and a cut parallel to a face gives a square of the same size.
quests.funFact: A loaf of bread shaped like a cube would give square slices.

quests.instruction: A ball of clay, which is a sphere, is cut with one flat cut. No matter where or at what angle it is cut, what shape is the cut surface?
quests.hint: A sphere is round in every direction.
quests.explanation: Every flat slice through a sphere is a circle, big or small, whatever the angle of the cut.
quests.funFact: An orange cut in half in any direction shows a circle.

quests.instruction: A cone is cut straight down from its tip through the middle of its base. What shape is the cut surface?
quests.hint: Picture the cone cut like a slice of cake from the top down to the bottom.
quests.explanation: The cut runs from the tip down to the base, so it has two slanted sides and a straight bottom, which is a triangle.
quests.funFact: A cone cut this way shows the same triangle as its side view.

quests.instruction: A brick lying flat is pressed into wet sand on its largest face. What shape is the mark?
quests.hint: The mark is the same shape as the face that was pressed.
quests.explanation: The largest face of a brick is a rectangle, so it leaves a rectangle-shaped mark.
quests.funFact: Bricks have been made from clay for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: A square pyramid is pressed into wet sand base first. What shape is the mark?
quests.hint: The mark is the same shape as the base.
quests.explanation: The base of a square pyramid is a square, so the mark is a square. The triangular sides do not touch the sand.
quests.funFact: The pyramids of Egypt were built on nearly perfect square bases.

quests.instruction: A cuboid has only flat faces with straight edges. Which print shape could it never make?
quests.hint: Think about what kind of edge the flat faces of a cuboid have.
quests.explanation: A cuboid has only flat faces with straight edges, so its prints are rectangles and sometimes squares. A circle needs a curved edge, which a cuboid does not have.
quests.funFact: To make a circle print you need a solid with a curved edge, like a cylinder or a cone.

quests.instruction: A tent has two triangle-shaped ends and three rectangular sides. What solid shape is it most like?
quests.hint: Look for the solid with two matching ends joined by flat sides.
quests.explanation: A solid with two matching triangle ends joined by rectangular sides is a triangular prism. A pyramid has one base and sides that meet at a point.
quests.funFact: Prisms are named after the shape of their matching ends.

quests.instruction: A chocolate bar box is a triangular prism. Looking at one end of the box, which flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: A triangular prism is named for the shape of its ends.
quests.explanation: The ends of a triangular prism are triangles, so the end of the box shows a triangle. The long sides are rectangles.
quests.funFact: Glass prisms shaped like this split white light into a rainbow.

quests.instruction: What is the difference between a pyramid and a triangular prism?
quests.correctAnswer: A pyramid comes to a point, and a prism has two matching ends
options: A pyramid comes to a point, and a prism has two matching ends
A pyramid is round, and a prism is flat
A pyramid has two matching ends, and a prism comes to a point
quests.hint: Think about the top of each solid: does it end in a point or in a matching shape?
quests.explanation: All the sides of a pyramid meet at one point at the top. A prism has the same shape at both ends and does not come to a point.
quests.funFact: A triangular prism has five faces: two triangles and three rectangles.

quests.instruction: An ice cream with a scoop is a cone with a ball of ice cream on top. Which two solid shapes does it use?
quests.hint: Think about the shape of the cone and the shape of the scoop.
quests.explanation: The cone holds a round scoop, so the ice cream is made of a cone and a sphere.
quests.funFact: Ice cream cones have been eaten for more than a hundred years.

quests.instruction: A new pencil with a sharp tip is a cylinder with a cone at one end. Which two flat shapes make up its side outline?
quests.hint: From the side, a cylinder looks like one flat shape and a cone looks like another.
quests.explanation: The cylinder part looks like a rectangle from the side, and the sharpened tip looks like a triangle, so the outline is a rectangle and a triangle.
quests.funFact: Sharpening a pencil turns the end of a cylinder into a cone.

quests.instruction: A snowman is built from three snowballs stacked up. How many different solid shapes are used?
quests.hint: Count kinds of shapes, not the number of snowballs.
quests.explanation: All three snowballs are spheres, so only one kind of solid shape is used.
quests.funFact: Snowmen are traditionally built with the largest snowball at the bottom for stability.

quests.instruction: A shop packs many items in a bag and wants them to fit together with no gaps. Which solid shape packs most tightly?
quests.hint: Think about which solid has flat faces that can sit against each other.
quests.explanation: Cubes have flat faces that fit against each other with no gaps. Spheres and cones are round, so they leave gaps.
quests.funFact: Sugar cubes are made as cubes so they stack tightly in a box.

quests.instruction: Why do shipping containers have a cuboid shape?
quests.correctAnswer: Cuboids stack and fit together with no wasted space
options: Cuboids stack and fit together with no wasted space
quests.hint: Think about how containers are stacked on a ship or a truck.
quests.explanation: Cuboids have flat faces that stack neatly in rows and columns, so none of the space between them is wasted.
quests.funFact: A large container ship can carry thousands of cuboid containers at once.

quests.instruction: Oranges are sold in a box shaped like a cuboid, but there are gaps between the oranges. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: Spheres cannot fit together without leaving gaps
options: The oranges are too small to fit
Spheres cannot fit together without leaving gaps
quests.hint: Think about how round things touch each other.
quests.explanation: Spheres touch each other at single points, so they cannot fill the space completely. A cuboid box has flat faces that fill space with no gaps.
quests.funFact: Even the best way to pack spheres still leaves about a quarter of the space empty.

quests.instruction: I have one flat circular face, one curved surface, and one pointed tip. What solid am I?
quests.hint: Count the flat faces and look for a point.
quests.explanation: A cone has one round flat base, a curved surface, and a point at the top. A cylinder has two flat faces and no point, and a sphere has no flat face.
quests.funFact: The tip of a cone is called its apex.

quests.instruction: I have a flat base and a pointed top, and I have no curved surface. What solid am I?
quests.hint: A pointed top and no curved surface rule out two of the choices.
quests.explanation: A pyramid has a flat base and flat triangular sides that meet at a point. A cone has a curved surface, and a triangular prism has no pointed top.
quests.funFact: The point where the sides of a pyramid meet is also called its apex.

quests.instruction: I have six rectangular faces, and my faces are not all squares. What solid am I?
quests.hint: Think about which solid has square faces only.
quests.explanation: A cuboid has six rectangular faces. A cube would need all six faces to be squares, and a cylinder has round ends.
quests.funFact: A matchbox is a cuboid.

quests.instruction: Which solid has faces that are squares and triangles?
quests.hint: Look for the solid with a square base and sloping sides.
quests.explanation: A square pyramid has one square face on the bottom and four triangular faces that meet at the top.
quests.funFact: A square pyramid has five faces in all.

quests.instruction: Which solid has faces that are rectangles and triangles?
quests.hint: Remember the tent: two triangle ends and rectangle sides.
quests.explanation: A triangular prism has two triangle faces and three rectangular faces. A cuboid has only rectangles, and a cone has a curved surface.
quests.funFact: Many camping tents are shaped like triangular prisms.

quests.instruction: Which solid always has faces that are all squares?
quests.hint: A square pyramid has some triangle faces, and a cuboid can have long faces.
quests.explanation: Every face of a cube is a square. A square pyramid has triangular faces, and a cuboid does not always have square faces.
quests.funFact: A puzzle cube with 3 rows of 3 by 3 is made of 27 small cubes.

quests.instruction: A sphere is cut exactly in half. Each half is called a hemisphere. What flat shape is the cut face?
quests.hint: Any flat cut through a sphere gives the same kind of shape.
quests.explanation: A flat cut through a sphere always makes a circle, and cutting through the center makes the biggest circle.
quests.funFact: Earth is divided into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres at the equator.

quests.instruction: A cylinder is sliced in half lengthwise, straight through the middle of both its circular ends. What shape is the cut face?
quests.hint: The cut runs along the whole length and across the full width.
quests.explanation: The cut face is as long as the cylinder and as wide as its circular ends, so it is a rectangle.
quests.funFact: Cutting a tube lengthwise and laying it flat also gives a rectangle.

quests.instruction: A square pyramid is sliced across, parallel to its base, about halfway up. What shape is the cut surface?
quests.hint: A slice parallel to the base is a smaller copy of the base.
quests.explanation: A slice parallel to the base is a smaller copy of the base shape, so it is a smaller square.
quests.funFact: The top of a pyramid that has been sliced off is another smaller pyramid.

quests.instruction: A solid has a circle as its top view and a triangle as its side view. What solid is it?
quests.hint: The top view tells you the base is round. Then check the side view.
quests.explanation: A cone seen from above is a circle and seen from the side is a triangle. A cylinder looks like a rectangle from the side, and a pyramid has a square top view.
quests.funFact: Engineers draw top, front, and side views to show exactly what a solid looks like.

quests.instruction: A solid has a square as its top view and a rectangle as its side view. Which solid could it be?
quests.correctAnswer: A tall cuboid with a square base
options: A tall cuboid with a square base
quests.hint: A square from above and a rectangle from the side point to a solid with flat faces.
quests.explanation: A tall cuboid with a square base looks like a square from above and a tall rectangle from the side. A cone and a sphere would both look round from above.
quests.funFact: Many pillars and posts are cuboids with square bases.

quests.instruction: A student says: A cube and a sphere are both solid shapes, so they both roll. Why is that wrong?
quests.correctAnswer: A cube has flat faces and edges that stop it from rolling smoothly
options: A cube is a flat shape
A cube has flat faces and edges that stop it from rolling smoothly
quests.hint: Think about what happens when you push a dice along a table.
quests.explanation: Being solid does not make something roll. A sphere rolls because it is smooth and round, but a cube has flat faces and edges, so it slides or tips.
quests.funFact: Wheels are circles or cylinders rather than cubes because round shapes roll smoothly.
